claims.text: Structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles under high-temperature service is governed by dynamic microstructural evolution and phase transformations.
Chemical stability of these nanoparticles under high-temperature service is governed by dynamic microstructural evolution and phase transformations.
High-temperature in situ TEM can directly reveal the relevant microstructural evolution and phase transformations.
The initial materials are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles synthesized using physical or chemical fabrication methods.
High-temperature in situ TEM characterization is proposed as the intervention used to observe microstructural evolution and phase transformations.
The relevant catalytic operating range is 773–1173 K.
The relevant thermoelectric operating range is 473–1923 K.
Dynamic microstructural evolution and phase transformations influence nanoparticle stability.
Dynamic microstructural evolution and phase transformations influence nanoparticle performance.
Observing these processes will improve understanding of synthesis–structure–property relationships.
Improved understanding will enable strategies for optimizing nanoparticle properties for catalytic and thermoelectric applications.
Current understanding of synthesis–structure–property relationships in these nanoparticles is limited.
